summary: The paper establishes sharp non-asymptotic sphere-packing bounds for (1,1)-criss-cross deletion codes by introducing an exact Levenshtein diagonal-and-swap deduplicated indel-pair bound and a three-tier deleted-slice run-decomposed sphere-packing theorem. These innovations slash Li-Sun-Ge overhead terms significantly (e.g., 53.3x at n=18, 90.2x at n=27) and lower strict finite-length redundancy thresholds across alphabets q=2,3,4,5,8. All 20 core structural theorems are formally verified in Lean 4.36.0 (0 sorry, 0 grind) and supported by zero-float exact-Q Python tests and 16 canonical certificates.
strengths: Exact Levenshtein diagonal-and-swap deduplication bound strictly improving Li-Sun-Ge Lemma 6 by a factor approaching q^2/(q-1)^2 (4x in binary).
Three-tier deleted-slice run-decomposed sphere-packing bound successfully eliminating the binary gap for n in [18, 26] and generalizing to rectangular arrays.
Complete formal verification in Lean 4.36.0 with zero sorry, zero grind, and zero Classical.choice, paired with exact-Q verification scripts and SHA-256 certificate manifests.
weaknesses: Scope is restricted to single (1,1)-criss-cross deletions (tr + tc <= 2), leaving multi-deletion extensions for future work.
Explicit code constructions matching the improved converse bounds for n in [18, 26] remain outside scope.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact Levenshtein diagonal-and-swap deduplicated single-indel confusable pair bound Pindel(q, L).
Three-tier deleted-slice run-decomposed sphere-packing bound with exact low-run family upper bound.
